sa_detail.why: complete (~3 points): A double bond is one region of electron density; VSEPR counts regions/domains rather than individual electron; Connects this to shape prediction around the central atom
sa_detail.answer: A double bond counts as one electron domain because it is one region of electron density around the central atom.

sa_detail.why: complete (~3 points): CO2 has two electron domains around carbon; Its electron-domain and molecular geometry are linear; Its bond angle is 180° and the Lewis structure has two C=O d
sa_detail.answer: CO2 is linear with a 180 bond angle because the central carbon has two double bonds, which is count as two electron domains, and no lone pairs.

pre.text_preview: Gears and Gear Ratios Quiz | Student: shiv | Generated: 8/8/2026, 9:08:03 pm |  | PART I: MULTIPLE CHOICE | 1. The gear that supplies the input motion is called the: |    A. Driven gear |    B. Driver gear |    C. Ra

sa_detail.why: complete (~3 points): Uses driven teeth ÷ driver teeth for the stated ratio conven; A larger driven gear turns more slowly than a smaller driver; A smaller driven gear turns faster than a larger driver
sa_detail.answer: The gear ratio determines speed, more driven teeth relative to the driver means slower output speed but more torque and vice versa.

sa_detail.why: complete (~3 points): An idler sits between driver and driven gears; It can change final rotation direction; It does not normally change the overall first-to-last ratio
sa_detail.answer: An idle gear reverses the direction of the driven gear to match the driver, but it does not change the overall gear ratio or speed.

sa_detail.why: minimal: Two or more different-sized gears rotate together on one sha
sa_detail.answer: A compound gear is two gears fixed on the same shaft so they spin together. This helps compound trains produce much bigger speed changes than a single gear pair.

sa_detail.why: partial: Find the ratio for each meshing stage; Multiply the stage ratios
sa_detail.answer: Multiply the ratio of each stage together to get the overall ratio.

sa_detail.why: complete (~3 points): Rack-and-pinion converts rotation and linear motion; Worm gear gives strong reduction and can resist back-driving; Bevel gear changes shaft direction, commonly by 90°
sa_detail.answer: Rack-and-pinion turns rotation into straight line motion, worm gear gives big speed reduction and locks in place, and bevel gear changes the direction of rotation between angled shafts.

pre.text_preview: Projectile Motion Quiz | Student: Charan | Generated: 8/8/2026, 5:24:43 pm |  | PART I: MULTIPLE CHOICE | 1. A projectile is an object that is: |    A. Moving only vertically |    B. Launched and then moves under g

sa_detail.why: partial: Horizontal motion has zero acceleration and constant velocit; Vertical motion has acceleration -g
sa_detail.answer: It means only gravity only affects vertical motion, so horizontal speed stays constant no matter whats happening vertically, the two only share the same time.

sa_detail.why: partial: Horizontal velocity remains constant; Vertical velocity decreases on ascent, becomes zero at the t
sa_detail.answer: Vertical velocity decreases going up, hits zero at the peak, then increases coming back down, while horizontal velocity stays constant the entire time.

sa_detail.why: partial: Both begin with the same initial vertical velocity; Both experience the same vertical acceleration -g
sa_detail.answer: Both balls start with zero vertical velocity and fall under the same gravity, so their vertical motion is identical no matter how fast one is moving sideways. Thats why they hit the ground together.

sa_detail.why: complete (~3 points): Vertical velocity is zero; Horizontal velocity remains nonzero and constant; Acceleration is still downward with magnitude g
sa_detail.answer: At the top, velocity is only horizontal since the vertical component is zero, but acceleration is still g downward the whole time.

sa_detail.why: partial: Use vertical motion to find flight time; Use horizontal motion x = v0x t to find range
sa_detail.answer: First use the vertical motion equation to solve for the time of flight, then plug that time into the horizontal equation to get how far the projectile travels.

sa_detail.answer:
Weathering = the breaking down of rock into smaller pieces at or near Earth’s surface.
Erosion = the movement of sediment from one place to another by water, wind, ice, or gravity.

sa_detail.why: minimal: Sediments were deposited in layers
sa_detail.answer: Sediments were deposited in layers over time, then buried and compressed.

sa_detail.why: partial: Water erodes softer shale below; Sandstone collapses, causing the canyon to widen
sa_detail.answer: Erosion removes the softer shale more quickly than the harder sandstone. This causes the sandstone above to collapse, making the canyon wider.
